_what: W1 changed a devkit-side file WHILE THIS RUN WAS SCORING. This file exists so the run's provenance is CORRECTED rather than silently false: bench_run.json.git.suite_code_blobs was captured at run start (cli.py:153) and therefore records the PRE-CHANGE blob for every arm, including arms scored AFTER the change.
change: RAM-guard Monitor default sustain 3 -> 60 samples (2 min); hard_floor_mb 2000.0 UNCHANGED
why_applied_mid_run: E1 MEASURED that sustain=3 killed a navhard CV run at 5,576/5,912 scored scenes on a six-second dip. THIS run is a navhard run and was exposed to exactly that death; waiting for it to finish would have left it exposed for ~2 more hours.
which_arms_are_affected: A running process does NOT re-read its source, and each arm is a FRESH subprocess. The arm in flight at the time of the change (CV, subprocess started 10:31:17 local) ran the PRE-change file to completion. Arms started AFTER the change run the POST-change file.
can_any_SCORE_differ: NO. The diff is 19 lines, entirely inside Monitor.__init__ (the RAM guard). The guard decides only WHEN TO ABORT; it is not in the scoring path, computes no metric and feeds nothing to the agent or the scorer. A completed arm is therefore bit-identical either way; the only possible difference is that an arm which WOULD have been aborted by a transient dip now completes.
verification: taniteval/tests/test_bench_suite_promotion.py -- 15 passed after the change; the binding re-promotion check (strip the marked W1 ADDITION blocks -> E1's origin byte-for-byte) passed BEFORE the file was written.
durable_fix_filed: suite_code_blobs is a RUN-START snapshot and cannot see a mid-run change. Filed to W1's COMMS as an integration item: capture the devkit-side blob PER ARM at launch, so this note becomes unnecessary.

THE_ASYMMETRY_THAT_MATTERS._why_this_field_exists: E1, 2026-09-20: a note recording ONLY 'no score can move' would leave a reader thinking the two arms were equivalent in every respect that matters. They were not. The difference is about SURVIVAL, not value.

abort_policy_per_arm.CV: sustain=3  (6 s) -- the PRE-change policy; the arm was already in flight and a running process does not re-read its source

THE_ASYMMETRY_THAT_MATTERS.consequence_if_CV_completes: its number is exactly as valid as STOP's -- the guard is not in the scoring path and cannot touch a metric.
THE_ASYMMETRY_THAT_MATTERS.what_CV_surviving_does_NOT_prove: ⛔ 'CV survived' is NOT evidence that sustain=3 was safe. The same policy killed E1's own navhard CV run at 5,576/5,912 -- 95 % -- on a dip lasting three samples. Survival under a policy is a draw from a distribution, not a property of the policy.
THE_ASYMMETRY_THAT_MATTERS.what_a_CV_death_would_have_meant: ⛔ it would have been the POLICY, not the DATA. A RAM_GUARD_ABORT on this arm must never be read as a scoring failure, a corpus problem or an arm defect -- scoring.py classifies it as RAM_GUARD_ABORT with retryable=true for exactly this reason.

hash_basis_reminder: Both blob pairs above are RAW-BYTE git blobs (no eol conversion). ⚠ `git hash-object` would print DIFFERENT ids for the same files and is BLIND to a pure line-ending change; devkit_patches() now carries BOTH, labelled.
superseded_by: PER-ARM capture, implemented 2026-09-20 on the orchestrator's ruling: scoring.score_arm now records devkit_side_blobs_at_launch + devkit_side_drift in <arm>.counts.json and WARNS at the moment a drift is seen. ⚠ THIS RUN PREDATES IT -- its parent process imported scoring.py before the change, so no arm of THIS run carries those fields. That is precisely why this file exists.
